correctness.rationale: The archival source supplies the common t-strict Schubert indexing and the exact ring scaling tau_lambda -> 2^{-ell_t(lambda)} sigma_lambda. In the nonmaximal range t>=1, the divisor class tau_1 is unscaled and equals c1(Q), hence the Pluecker hyperplane maps to the symplectic Pluecker hyperplane. The unique top partition has r parts above t, so comparing the coefficients of the top Schubert class after multiplying by the complementary power of the hyperplane gives deg_B = 2^{r-ell_t(lambda)} deg_C. The ambient ratio is independently checked from the type B and type C Weyl products.

value.rationale: Projective degree is the basic enumerative count of complementary general Pluecker hyperplanes on a Schubert variety. The theorem gives one formula for every corresponding Schubert variety in two equal-dimensional classical homogeneous spaces, showing that the entire odd arithmetic of these enumerative counts is identical and that the discrepancy is controlled by the intrinsic partition statistic ell_t(lambda). It upgrades an ambient-variety comparison to a complete Schubert-family dictionary and isolates exactly how far each stratum lies from odd-part equality.
